permutationLabel: Young atopic man, recurrent impaction (resolved) — eosinophilic oesophagitis
summary: 23-year-old man with asthma and eczema: years of intermittent solid-food sticking and three self-resolving bolus episodes; eating slowly. BSG 2022: OGD with ≥6 biopsies from at least two levels; EoE must be on the differential.

inputs.hpi: Since his teens, meat and bread intermittently stick in the chest; he chews carefully and drinks a lot with meals. Three episodes where food got completely stuck for an hour and then passed. Currently swallowing normally. Asthma and eczema; hay fever. Weight steady. Heartburn rarely.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected eosinophilic oesophagitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Intermittent solid-food dysphagia with recurrent bolus impaction in a young atopic man — suspected eosinophilic oesophagitis. OGD with oesophageal biopsies.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: No eosinophilic oesophagitis disease in PANE or symptom inference (only a key point in the oesophageal_stricture protocol). | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): not in top 5 of ios.bayes: 1. Gastro-oesophageal Reflux Disease | 2. Oesophageal / Gastric Carcinoma | 3. Upper GI Bleeding (Peptic Ulcer) | 4. Oesophageal Web / Plummer-Vinson Syndrome | 5. Acute Coronary Syndrome
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add an EoE node (young, atopy, intermittent solid dysphagia, bolus episodes) and a K20.0 protocol (≥6 biopsies from ≥2 levels; PPI / budesonide / diet; dilatation).

emergencyLevel.note: Dysphagia at any age → urgent OGD (NG12), but not an emergency when swallowing now.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Emergency now: "Systemic red flag symptom" and "Dysphagia" red flags plus a 2-week-wait cancer screen labelled "colorectal" (cancer-screening.ts operator-precedence bug; see findings).
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: cancer-screening.ts: parenthesise the colorectal cancerType condition (c.met && (… || … )); dysphagia should give priority, not emergency_now, when the patient is swallowing.

mustInclude.note: EoE is a histological diagnosis; a normal-looking oesophagus without biopsies misses it.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): no investigation matched among 5 (ios.pipeline.voi, ios.radiation)

guideline.name: BSG/BSPGHAN joint consensus guidelines — diagnosis and management of eosinophilic oesophagitis in children and adults
guideline.section: Suspect EoE in dysphagia or food bolus obstruction, especially young atopic men; OGD with at least 6 biopsies from at least two oesophageal levels; first-line PPI, topical steroid (orodispersible budesonide) or dietary therapy; dilatation for strictures
guideline.citation: Dhar A, Haboubi HN, Attwood SE, et al. Gut. 2022;71:1459–1487.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (oesophageal and stomach cancer)
guideline.section: Dysphagia at any age: urgent direct-access OGD
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (last updated 2023).

rationale: Young/atopic permutation of the food-bolus case. The key safety-relevant output is that biopsies are taken at OGD (EoE is missed when the oesophagus is only looked at). PANE has no EoE node, so this also measures coverage.
